title: Control Flow: Loops
relevance: Loops and Python’s for/while-else with break are staple OA and campus SDE checks of basic control-flow fluency.

phases.goal: Establish what a loop is and how for with range or direct iteration over sequences works.

must_hit.point: A loop repeats a block of code as long as a condition is met or for every item in a sequence.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate defines a loop as repeated execution tied to a condition or walking a sequence.

must_hit.point: range(start, stop, step) yields integers from start up to but not including stop, advancing by step; a negative step counts downward.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They state stop is exclusive and mention negative step for countdown.

must_hit.point: for i in range(10, 0, -1) runs from 10 down to 1 because stop 0 is excluded.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They walk the range(10, 0, -1) example and say 0 is not printed.

must_hit.point: A for loop can iterate an iterable directly—string (one character), list, or tuple—without an index.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They mention for over 'Delhi', a list, or a tuple yielding elements one by one.

probes: What does range(start, stop, step) produce, and what happens with a negative step?
How does for iterate a string versus a list or tuple?

hints.1: Think about what stop means in range and whether the endpoint is included.
hints.2: Separate range-based counting from walking elements of an iterable.
hints.3: range excludes stop; for x in 'Delhi' yields D, e, l, h, i one character at a time.

phases.goal: Explain for…else and while…else and how break decides whether else runs.

must_hit.point: A loop else runs only if the for iterable is exhausted or the while condition becomes False.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They say else runs on natural completion, not on every exit.

must_hit.point: If the loop ends early via break, Python skips the else block entirely.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They link break to skipping else; many rename else to no_break.

must_hit.point: The same else rule applies to while: natural False runs else; break skips it.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They give or describe a while countdown that finishes and then runs else.

probes: When does a for…else or while…else block execute, and when is it skipped?
Walk through finding a value in a list with break and else.

hints.1: Compare finishing every iteration to exiting early.
hints.2: Map the dark-room search: break when found; else means the search never broke.
hints.3: else runs only on natural finish; break unconditionally skips else.

phases.goal: Judge when loop else is meaningful versus redundant after the loop.

must_hit.point: Loop else pairs naturally with break; read it as “if the loop never broke, then…”.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They treat else as the no-break path paired with an in-loop break.

must_hit.point: Without a break inside, else is equivalent to code after the loop and adds nothing.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They say bare else with no break is redundant with post-loop code.

probes: When would you attach else to a loop instead of putting code after it?
Why is for…else easy to misuse if you come from languages without it?

hints.1: Ask whether the loop body can break.
hints.2: Useful when success is break and failure is completing without break.
hints.3: No break → else equals code after the loop; with break → else is the no-break failure path.

phases.goal: Apply break-plus-else to search and nested prime filtering.

must_hit.point: Classic search: break when the target is found so else is skipped; if the loop completes, else reports the target was absent.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They describe found→break skips else; absent→else prints the not-found message.

must_hit.point: In the primes pattern, the inner for tries divisors; a hit breaks; only when no divisor is found does the inner else run and print i.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They say else is on the inner for and prints primes that survived the divisor test.

must_hit.point: In that primes example the inner divisor loop is for j in range(2, i).
must_hit.evidence_hint: They name range(2, i) as the potential-divisor scan.

probes: How would you use for…else to search a list and report not found without a flag?
Explain how nested for…else prints primes in a range.

hints.1: Search: break on hit; else means never broke.
hints.2: Primes: composite breaks the inner loop; prime lets inner else print.
hints.3: Inner else is attached to the divisor for; it fires once per i that never broke.

tradeoffs.topic: loop else with break vs code after the loop
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Else is the no-break path and pairs with break for search-style control flow; without any break, else is the same as code after the loop and adds nothing.

tradeoffs.topic: Python loop else vs if/else intuition from other languages
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Loop else is unique to Python and does not mean “condition was false” like if/else; it means the loop finished naturally without break, which many remember by renaming else to no_break.

gotchas.trap: Reading loop else like if/else—as running when the loop condition failed in the usual sense.
gotchas.correction: Else runs only if the for iterable is exhausted or while becomes False; break skips else entirely.

gotchas.trap: Attaching else to a loop that never breaks and expecting special behavior.
gotchas.correction: Without a break, else is equivalent to code after the loop and adds nothing.

gotchas.trap: In nested prime printing, attaching else to the outer for instead of the inner divisor for.
gotchas.correction: Else must be on the inner for so it fires once per i that survived the divisor test—the primes.
